# Frontend Scaffolder

**Principle:** boilerplate is generated by the CLI/config, not the LLM. Run these
steps, then fill in feature-specific code.

## 0. Where the app goes (fixed repo folder structure)

Inputs: `NAME` — the project name in kebab-case (e.g. `acme-billing`), the same
one the backend uses for `backend/<name>-api`.

```text
<repo>/
├── backend/<name>-api/          # `solution-scaffolder`
├── frontend/
│   ├── <name>-ui/               # the main UI — this skill's default target
│   └── <name>-<ui>-ui/          # a separate UI — only when the user asks for one
├── docs/                        # all documentation and related files
└── docker-compose.yml
```

- Every UI is its **own folder under `frontend/`**: the main one is `<name>-ui`,
  any other is `<name>-<ui>-ui`, where `<ui>` is **the name the user asked for**,
  kebab-cased — `admin` → `<name>-admin-ui`, `partner portal` →
  `<name>-partner-portal-ui`. `admin` is only an example, not a fixed name; never
  rename what the user asked for, and ask if they gave no name. Never scaffold at the repo root or directly
  into `frontend/`.
- A separate UI (admin panel, back-office, partner portal, anything else) is
  created **only on request** — not "because we will need one eventually". It is a
  full app of its own: run §1–§8 again in `frontend/<name>-<ui>-ui`. Apps do not
  import from each other.
- Below, `<app>` is that folder name (`<name>-ui`, `<name>-<ui>-ui`) and
  all paths (`src/...`) are relative to `frontend/<app>/`.

## 1. Create the app
```bash
mkdir -p frontend && cd frontend
npm create vite@latest <app> -- --template react-ts     # <app> = $NAME-ui
cd <app>
npm i @tanstack/react-query @tanstack/react-router zustand zod react-hook-form @hookform/resolvers
npm i -D vitest @testing-library/react @testing-library/user-event jsdom msw \
       @playwright/test eslint prettier eslint-plugin-boundaries eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y \
       eslint-plugin-import @typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin @typescript-eslint/parser \
       tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite
```

## 2. TypeScript strict (`tsconfig.json`)
```jsonc
{ "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true, "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true, "noImplicitOverride": true,
    "verbatimModuleSyntax": true, "baseUrl": "src",
    "paths": { "@/*": ["*"] } } }
```

## 3. Folder structure (create up front)
```bash
mkdir -p src/app src/components src/shared/api src/shared/hooks src/shared/lib src/features
```
```text
src/app/         providers.tsx, router.tsx, App.tsx
src/components/   shared UI primitives
src/shared/api/   httpClient.ts (typed fetch + auth/refresh + Zod error shape)
src/features/     one folder per domain (see feature-architecture skill)
```

## 4. ESLint encodes the architecture (the programmatic guard)
```jsonc
// boundaries: features can't import siblings; shared can't import features
"plugins": ["boundaries", "jsx-a11y", "import", "@typescript-eslint"],
"settings": { "boundaries/elements": [
  { "type": "app", "pattern": "src/app/*" },
  { "type": "feature", "pattern": "src/features/*", "capture": ["name"] },
  { "type": "component", "pattern": "src/components/*" },
  { "type": "shared", "pattern": "src/shared/*" } ] },
"rules": {
  "boundaries/element-types": ["error", { "default": "disallow", "rules": [
    { "from": "feature",   "allow": ["shared", "component", ["feature", { "name": "${from.name}" }]] },
    { "from": "component", "allow": ["shared"] },
    { "from": "app",       "allow": ["feature", "component", "shared"] },
    { "from": "shared",    "allow": ["shared"] } ] }],
  "import/no-cycle": "error",
  "@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any": "error"
}
```
> This is the frontend analogue of the backend's NetArchTest: boundaries are a
> failing lint error, not a convention.

## 5. Global providers (`src/app/providers.tsx`)
```tsx
const queryClient = new QueryClient({ defaultOptions: { queries: { staleTime: 30_000 } } });
export function Providers({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>{children}</QueryClientProvider>;
}
```
Wire the router + `Providers` in `App.tsx`; keep `src/app/` thin and structural.

## 6. Test + MSW setup
- `vitest.config.ts` with `environment: 'jsdom'`, a `setupTests.ts` that starts the
  MSW server. `src/shared/test/` for render helpers + handlers.
- `npx playwright install` + a `playwright.config.ts` for E2E.

## 7. Scripts + verify
```jsonc
"scripts": {
  "dev":"vite","build":"tsc -b && vite build","preview":"vite preview",
  "lint":"eslint .","typecheck":"tsc --noEmit","test":"vitest run","e2e":"playwright test" }
```
```bash
npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run build   # green skeleton before any feature work
```

## 8. Join the docker-compose stack (never leave `up` running half a system)

**Check first:** is there a `docker-compose.yml` at the repo root?

```bash
ls ../../docker-compose.y*ml 2>/dev/null   # from frontend/<app>: backend already set up local dev?
```

**If yes — add this frontend to it.** The backend's stack is the single source of
truth for local dev (`docs/backend/ARCHITECTURE.md` §10.1, `local-dev-environment`
skill — load it for the canonical service block and Dockerfile). You add:
- `frontend/<app>/Dockerfile` with a `dev` target (Vite dev server) and a default
  target (build → nginx) for deploys;
- a `frontend` service: `build: { context: ./frontend/<app>, target: dev }`, port
  **5173** published, `./frontend/<app>` bind-mounted plus an anonymous
  `/app/node_modules` volume, `depends_on: [api]`;
- `server: { host: true, port: 5173, watch: { usePolling: true } }` in
  `vite.config.ts` so it listens in the container and sees host edits;
- the README URL table row.

Two things to get right, both of which fail silently otherwise:
- `VITE_API_URL` must be **browser-reachable** (`http://localhost:8080`), not
  `http://api:8080` — the request comes from the host browser, which cannot
  resolve compose service names.
- The API's Development CORS policy must allow `http://localhost:5173`. Ask the
  backend side to add it (`security-engineer` owns CORS) if it is missing.

Do **not** create a second compose file, and do not put the frontend on port 3000
— Grafana already publishes it.

**A second UI** joins the same file as its own service, named after its role
(`<ui>-ui` for `frontend/<name>-<ui>-ui` — e.g. `admin-ui`), on the next free port (**5174**,
then 5175, ...) — set the same port in its `vite.config.ts`, and have the API's
Development CORS policy allow that origin too.

**If there is no compose file yet:** skip this and say so — the backend's
`local-dev-environment` skill adds the frontend when it creates the stack.

Verify: `docker compose up -d --build` → `http://localhost:5173` renders **and its
API calls succeed in the browser devtools**, not just the page loading.
